items.response:
That's lovely, a bit teary means the flowers landed. Thanks for telling me, and take your time deciding tonight.
Action: Note that your mom's birthday is November 3 and that you send flowers through the Mumbai florist and call her that morning, so I can remind you ahead of time next year.

Sorry about the heel. Given the plantar fasciitis you had earlier this year, it is worth getting looked at before it settles in. I'll avoid Saturday mornings if Leo's swim lesson at 10:00 still stands, so a later Saturday slot or a weekday after work.
Action: Look for physio openings next week after work or on Saturday after swimming, check them against your calendar, and bring you the best two options to confirm before I book. I'll mention the earlier foot issue in the booking note.

I only have a note that you once asked me for a summary of a podcast episode about pricing for B2B APIs. I don't have the show or episode title, and I don't want to guess and send Aisha the wrong one.
Action: Search our earlier chats for that summary and pull the episode name and link; if I can't find it, I'll ask you for the show name.

On it. I'll open the instant payouts readiness doc and go through the open comments, the linked tickets, and anything still hanging from the last review.
Action: Read the doc in Notion, then send you a short list of unresolved items grouped as comments, tickets and review follow-ups, with who owns each.

That's rough, the Sunday evening dread is real, and an extra hour doesn't fix it. Let's make tomorrow smaller so it feels less heavy.
Action: Pull together the two or three things that actually matter tomorrow, including the pending call about the payout edge cases, and send them as a short list so you can switch off for tonight.

Here's a draft for #payouts-launch:
'Reminder: the beta retro is Thursday at 2pm in room 4B. Please add your sticky notes to the Miro board before then. Thanks all!'
Action: Hold it as a draft until you say go, then post it in #payouts-launch.

That sounds stressful, and spinning when you can't reach her is completely understandable. You're probably right that it's her phone, since you said it is always dying, and a missed weekend call doesn't change that.
Action: Suggest trying her once more later today, and if you'd like, I can help you think of someone who could check on her in the meantime. I'll leave a reminder for this evening so you aren't left watching the phone.

Good idea. Since the team already works in Linear, Slack and Notion, I'd make one Notion database as the single intake and triage it weekly. Starting columns: Merchant, Source (support, sales, reply to update), Date received, Summary, Verbatim quote, Category (bug, UX, feature request, pricing), Severity, Owner, Status (new, triaged, linked to ticket, closed), Linear ticket link.
Action: Create that database in Notion with a weekly triage view and a short 'how to log' note at the top, then send you the link to share with the team.

Here's one: 'Happy birthday, Tom! Thanks for being a steady, kind boss, hope you get a great day and a proper break.'
Action: Give you one or two shorter or warmer variants if you want to compare, then you can paste your pick into the card.

Ha, 'obviously' is the perfect answer. A paleontologist who runs a pizza oven sounds like a fine plan, and Sam walked right into that one.
Action: Save this in Leo's memory notes, with the date, if you'd like. Just say the word.

I don't have a record of that from what I can see right now, so I can't say either way and I don't want to guess.
Action: Search your emails, receipts and order history for a furnace filter purchase or pickup from before Christmas, and tell you what I find.

Happy to find one that is a calmer pumpkin patch than the big-name ones. I'll keep it within 45 minutes of home so you can leave about 1:30.
Action: Look up pumpkin patches in range, check today's hours and how busy they usually get, and send you two or three options with drive times. I'll check that nothing on your calendar clashes.

Good call, a Zoom link should be easier for her than WhatsApp video. I don't have the day and time of this week's call in front of me, so I'll check your calendar before I put it in the text.
Action: Create the Zoom meeting, then text your mom the link with a short, calm note on how to join. I'll show you the text first if the time isn't clear on your calendar.

Got it, I'll handle it without checking back. I'm looking for a well-reviewed hotel in or near the Plateau under $250 a night for Fri 6 Feb to Sun 8 Feb, and I'll lean towards one with free cancellation in case plans shift.
Action: Search, book the best match, and send you the confirmation with the total, address and cancellation terms.

That's lovely, a bit teary means the flowers landed. Thanks for telling me, and take your time deciding tonight.
Action: Note that your mom's birthday is November 3 and that you send flowers through the Mumbai florist and call her that morning, so I can remind you ahead of time next year.

Will do, shorter replies from here.
Action: Keep answers brief today.

I'll tell Marcus you'll think about it. Here's a draft for the Okafors, in Canadian spelling:
'Dear Grace and Daniel, thank you so much for having us for Christmas in Ottawa. Your home was warm and welcoming, the meals were wonderful, and we were thrilled to be sent home with so many leftovers. We had a lovely time and are grateful for everything you did. With love from all three of us.'
Action: Reply to Marcus that you'll think about it, and wait for your edits on the card, such as adding all three names.

From what I have, you leave on TAP TP260 on Sun 20 Dec at 22:10 and return on TP259 on Sat 2 Jan, so I'd block Mon 21 Dec through Fri 1 Jan as OOO, and an early leave on Thu 10 Dec for Morse Street's winter concert at 6:30 pm (you told Tom you'd leave at 5:00). I'd also ask Tom whether Fri 18 Dec, Leo's last school day, needs anything. I don't have a record of what you did on the snow day; the only note says you asked for indoor games on 27 Jan, not what you ended up doing.
Action: Add the OOO block and the early leave to the team calendar as drafts for your check before Friday, and look through your chats from that day to see if the snow day activity shows up.

Sure, I'll text Hannah. I don't have the exact July dates in front of me, so I'll check your calendar and include them rather than guess.
Action: Send Hannah a friendly text asking if she can feed and walk Biscuit while you're away, mention that you'll pay, and ask what rate or arrangement works for her. I'll tell you as soon as she answers.

Happy early birthday to Leo. Two things I'll build in. Leo has a skating lesson at 10:30 on Saturdays through 13 March, so Sat 23 Jan clashes with the morning unless the party is in the afternoon. And with his cashew and pistachio allergy, I'll ask Wonder Workshop how they handle outside food, cake and nut-free options.
Action: Check Wonder Workshop on Queen East for party packages for twelve kids on that Saturday afternoon, with prices, time slots and allergy policy, and report back.

I don't have your December travel or school dates on hand, so I'd rather not guess what to block, and I don't have a record of the snow day either.
Action: Check your calendar for December trips, school events and days off, then send you a proposed list of OOO and early-leave days to confirm before Friday. For Leo's 'that thing', could you or Sam remember a detail? I'll also search old chats and photos from last winter for clues.

I'll tell Marcus you'll think about it. Here's a draft for the Okafors:
'Dear Grace and Daniel, thank you so much for having us for Christmas in Ottawa. We loved every minute, from the warm welcome to the wonderful meals, and the leftovers you sent us home with kept us fed for days. We are so grateful. With love from all three of us.'
Action: Reply to Marcus that you'll think about it, then adjust the card note with your edits, such as adding names.

I'll set those up as tentative: prep Mon 15 and Tue 16 March, the offsite Wed 17 and Thu 18, and 'roadmap deck due' on Fri 12 March. One thing to flag gently: 18 March is around the anniversary of your father's passing, when you usually prefer a lighter schedule. Do you want to keep Thursday as is, or ask Tom if you can leave early or join remotely?
Action: Create the tentative holds now, and leave Thursday as a note for you to decide on.

That sounds perfect, you've earned it. I'll keep things quiet.
Action: Hold all non-urgent messages and work notifications until later and only interrupt you for something truly urgent.

Here's a draft for #payouts-launch:
'Reminder: the beta retro is Thursday at 2pm in room 4B. Please add your sticky notes to the Miro board before then. Thanks all!'
Action: Hold it as a draft until you say go, then post it in #payouts-launch.

Glad it landed. Riya the poet has a nice ring to it.
Action: Nothing needed; I can do one for Fridays if the pinned streak continues.

Glad it landed. Riya the poet has a nice ring to it.
Action: Nothing needed; I can do one for Fridays if the pinned streak continues.

Understood, I'll talk through the number with you whenever you want. For the standup, I'll pull every open risk for the payouts launch from Linear and put them into one Notion doc, grouped by severity and owner, with dates in ISO format since it's a work document.
Action: Query Linear for open payouts launch risks, build the Notion doc, and send you the link to review before standup.

A few ideas for Sam's birthday on March 22: he'd probably love a quiet dinner at home over a restaurant, so cook something vegetarian (no fish or seafood) he likes. Gift-wise, a vintage Penguin paperback or two, or the Fellow Ode coffee grinder he's wanted for a while. For the anniversary I have two dates on file, June 8 and June 16, so I'm not sure which is right. Could you confirm? Then I can book a dinner out without Leo well ahead of time.
Action: Wait for the anniversary date, then draft a plan with a gift shortlist, a menu and a reservation for the anniversary.

Here's one for Ellie: 'Dogs hear sounds much higher and from much farther away than we do, so Biscuit heard the siren long before we did. When he howls, he's singing along, the way wolves sing to talk to each other. He isn't scared, he's saying hello to the fire truck!'
Action: Offer a shorter version if you want one, and add a reminder for tomorrow to tell Ellie.
